description: This topic explores the meaning and functions of money, the difference between needs and wants, budgeting, saving, family income and expenditure, banking, and the responsible use of money.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following best describes money?

options.text: Any item that is expensive to produce
Anything generally accepted as a means of payment for goods and services
Only the paper notes printed by a government
Goods that are exchanged directly without value

mcq.explanation: Money is anything that is widely and generally accepted by people as a means of payment for goods, services, and the settlement of debts.

mcq.questionText: What was the main system of exchanging goods used before money was invented?
mcq.explanation: The barter system involved exchanging goods directly for other goods without the use of money.

mcq.questionText: Which function of money allows a person to keep their wealth for future use?
mcq.explanation: As a store of value, money can be saved and used later because it keeps its purchasing power over time.

mcq.questionText: Money used to compare the prices of different goods is performing its function as a:
mcq.explanation: As a measure of value, money provides a common standard for expressing and comparing the prices of goods and services.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is an example of a need rather than a want?
mcq.explanation: Clean drinking water is a basic requirement for survival, making it a need, while the others are wants.

mcq.questionText: A plan that shows expected income and expenditure over a period of time is called a:
mcq.explanation: A budget is a financial plan that estimates income and how that income will be spent over a given period.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is the most common form of money used in everyday transactions in Tanzania?
mcq.explanation: Notes and coins (currency) issued by the central bank are the everyday form of money used in Tanzania.

mcq.questionText: Which institution is responsible for issuing notes and coins in Tanzania?
mcq.explanation: The Bank of Tanzania is the central bank with the sole authority to issue the country's currency.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a source of family income?
mcq.explanation: Wages and salaries earned from employment are a major source of family income, while the others are forms of expenditure.

mcq.questionText: Setting aside part of your income for future use is known as:
mcq.explanation: Saving is the act of keeping aside a portion of income instead of spending it, so it can be used later.

mcq.questionText: Why is it important for a family to prepare a budget?

options.text: To make sure all income is spent immediately
To help control spending and avoid wasting money
To increase the number of debts
To stop the family from saving

mcq.explanation: A budget helps a family plan and control its spending, prioritise needs, and avoid wasting money.

mcq.questionText: When the amount a family spends is greater than the income it receives, this situation is called a:
mcq.explanation: A deficit budget occurs when expenditure exceeds income, which can lead to borrowing or debt.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is an example of responsible use of money?

options.text: Spending all your money on wants
Buying only what you can afford and saving the rest
Borrowing money to buy luxuries you do not need

mcq.explanation: Responsible use of money means living within your means, prioritising needs, and saving for the future.

mcq.questionText: A document issued by a seller as proof that a buyer has paid for goods is called a:
mcq.explanation: A receipt is a written acknowledgement that payment has been received for goods or services.

mcq.questionText: Which financial institution mainly collects small savings and gives loans to its members, who are also its owners?
mcq.explanation: A SACCOS is a member-owned cooperative that mobilises members' savings and provides them with affordable loans.

fib.questionText: The direct exchange of goods for other goods without using money is called the _____ system.
fib.explanation: Under the barter system people traded goods directly, for example exchanging maize for fish.

fib.questionText: When money is used to buy goods and services, it is performing its function as a medium of _____.
fib.explanation: As a medium of exchange, money is accepted in return for goods and services.

fib.questionText: Things that are necessary for survival, such as food, water, and shelter, are called _____.
fib.explanation: Needs are basic requirements that a person must have to live, unlike wants which are optional.

fib.questionText: A written financial plan of expected income and expenditure is known as a _____.
fib.explanation: A budget helps people plan how to use their income wisely.

fib.questionText: The act of keeping part of one's income aside for future use is called _____.
fib.explanation: Saving allows a person to meet future needs and emergencies.

fib.questionText: The central bank that issues currency in Tanzania is the Bank of _____.
fib.explanation: The Bank of Tanzania is the only institution allowed to print and issue the national currency.

fib.questionText: The money a family spends on goods and services is known as _____.
fib.explanation: Expenditure refers to the outflow of money used to pay for needs and wants.

fib.questionText: A budget in which income is equal to expenditure is called a _____ budget.
fib.explanation: In a balanced budget, total income exactly matches total expenditure.

fib.questionText: Money saved in a bank usually earns an extra payment called _____.
fib.explanation: Banks pay interest to savers as a reward for keeping money in a savings account.

fib.questionText: The metal form of money of small value, such as fifty or one hundred shillings, is called a _____.
fib.explanation: Coins are the metal form of currency, usually used for smaller amounts of money.

tf.questionText: Money acts as a store of value because it can be saved and used in the future.
tf.explanation: Money keeps its purchasing power over time, so it can be stored and spent later.

tf.questionText: Under the barter system, goods were exchanged using paper notes and coins.
tf.explanation: The barter system involved exchanging goods directly for other goods, not using money.

tf.questionText: A want is something a person can live without, unlike a need.
tf.explanation: Wants are desires that improve comfort or enjoyment but are not essential for survival.

tf.questionText: Spending more money than you earn is a sign of good financial management.
tf.explanation: Spending more than you earn leads to debt and is poor financial management.

tf.questionText: Only commercial banks in Tanzania have the authority to print currency notes.
tf.explanation: Only the central bank, the Bank of Tanzania, has the authority to issue currency.

tf.questionText: Preparing a budget helps a family to prioritise its needs before its wants.
tf.explanation: A budget guides spending so that essential needs are met before money is spent on wants.

tf.questionText: Saving money helps a family to deal with emergencies and future needs.
tf.explanation: Savings provide a financial cushion for unexpected expenses and future plans.

tf.questionText: A receipt is given to a buyer as proof that payment has been made.
tf.explanation: A receipt confirms that money has been received for goods or services.

tf.questionText: Borrowing money to buy luxuries you do not need is an example of responsible use of money.
tf.explanation: Responsible use of money means avoiding unnecessary debt and living within your means.

tf.questionText: Wages, salaries, and profits from business are examples of sources of family income.
tf.explanation: These are common ways families earn the money they use for daily living.

summary.correctAnswer: Anything generally accepted as a means of payment for goods and services.
summary.explanation: Money makes trade easier than the barter system.

summary.correctAnswer: Medium of exchange, measure of value, store of value, and standard of deferred payment.
summary.explanation: These functions show why money is useful in an economy.

summary.correctAnswer: Notes (paper money) and coins (metal money), plus bank money.
summary.explanation: Currency is the most common everyday form of money.

summary.correctAnswer: Needs are essential for survival, while wants are desires that are not essential.
summary.explanation: Needs should be satisfied before wants.

summary.correctAnswer: A plan of expected income and expenditure over a period of time.
summary.explanation: A budget guides wise spending and saving.

summary.correctAnswer: Wages, salaries, business profits, farming, and rent.
summary.explanation: These are ways families earn money for daily needs.

summary.correctAnswer: Setting aside part of one's income for future use.
summary.explanation: Savings help with emergencies and future goals.

summary.correctAnswer: It provides for emergencies, future needs, investment, and reduces dependence on borrowing.

summary.questionText: Role of the Bank of Tanzania
summary.correctAnswer: It is the central bank that issues currency and controls the country's money supply.
summary.explanation: Only the central bank can issue notes and coins.

summary.correctAnswer: Spending within your means, prioritising needs, budgeting, and saving regularly.
summary.explanation: It helps avoid debt and build financial stability.

hoq.questionText: A family earns 600,000 shillings per month but spends 750,000 shillings. Which action would best improve their financial situation in the long term?

options.text: Borrow more money each month to cover the gap
Prepare a budget, cut spending on wants, and look for extra income
Stop saving completely so all money can be spent
Spend more on luxuries to feel better

hoq.explanation: The family has a deficit, so reducing unnecessary spending through a budget and increasing income is the sustainable solution, while borrowing only worsens debt.

hoq.questionText: Two students each receive the same pocket money. Juma spends all of his on snacks, while Asha saves part of hers in a SACCOS each week. After one year, why is Asha in a better financial position?

options.text: Because saving has built her a fund that may also earn interest
Because spending all money always increases wealth
Because snacks are a form of long-term investment
Because pocket money loses value when it is saved

hoq.explanation: Regular saving accumulates a fund over time and may earn interest, giving Asha financial security that Juma lacks because he spent everything.

hoq.questionText: Why would a country that returns to a pure barter system likely struggle compared with one that uses money?

options.text: Barter makes it easier to store wealth for the future
Barter requires a double coincidence of wants, making trade slow and difficult
Barter provides a single standard for measuring all values
Barter allows easy payment of debts over time

hoq.explanation: Barter requires both parties to want what the other offers (a double coincidence of wants), which makes trade inefficient, whereas money solves this problem.
